title: At SFO, some shuttle operators faced curb fees higher than the fare

beats.text: At SFO, a shuttle’s curb fee could exceed a passenger’s entire fare.

visual.sub: The same curb fee formula produced very different costs per rider

beats.text: The airport’s consultant found three companies under $5 per departing passenger.

visual.kicker: The same curb fee formula produced very different costs per rider

beats.text: Four other companies faced $10 or more.
The typical fare ranged from $13 to $17.

visual.kicker: The same curb fee formula produced very different costs per rider

beats.text: The airport counted vans leaving the staging lot.

visual.kicker: The airport counted vehicles leaving the lot

beats.text: Ten operators shared a monthly bill of $191,360 in January 2013.

visual.label: The airport counted vehicles leaving the lot

beats.text: By 2016, Airport Express had sued over the curb rules.

visual.kicker: SFO defended the curb design and the judge dismissed the challenge

beats.text: A federal judge dismissed its amended challenge with prejudice.

visual.kicker: SFO defended the curb design and the judge dismissed the challenge

beats.text: On September 6, three proposed contracts reached the Commission.

visual.kicker: Three proposed contracts never received an award

beats.text: It rejected all proposals after smaller operators raised concerns.
Airport Express voluntarily dismissed its appeal.

visual.kicker: Three proposed contracts never received an award

beats.text: By 2021, pandemic-era shared-ride activity had fallen 97.9 percent.

visual.kicker: The pandemic changed demand before the curb rules changed again

beats.text: What operators pay per passenger today still takes individual permits and boarding records.
